images.title: From tiny to big: the units of weight
images.purpose: Show the five units of weight in order, from the milligram to the tonne, with the fact that links each pair.
images.composition: A title, five boxes in a row from the smallest to the biggest unit joined by four arrows, a fact under each arrow, and a banner.
images.exact_structure: Plain white frame, 1456 by 816. TITLE at the top left, x 60, y 70: the text From tiny to big (48 px, bold, dark #1F2937). FIVE BOXES in a row at y 280 to 420, each a rounded rectangle 220 by 140 px with a 4 px outline #1F2937, left edges at x 40, 329, 618, 907, 1196, filled from the smallest to the biggest unit with pale teal #CCE5F2, #99CBE5, #66B2D8, #3399CB and #0072B2 (the last with white text), holding the unit names milligram (mg), gram (g), kilogram (kg), quintal, tonne (36 px, bold, dark #1F2937). FOUR ARROWS, each a thick dark #1F2937 arrow 60 px long from one box to the next, pointing right, at y 350 between the boxes (arrow centres at x 294, 584, 872, 1162). FACT TAGS under the arrows at y 470 to 530, centred on the arrows, 36 px, dark: 1,000 mg = 1 g; 1,000 g = 1 kg; 100 kg = 1 quintal; 10 quintals = 1 tonne. BANNER at the bottom, y 640 to 720, a rounded rectangle 760 by 80 px centred at x 728 with a 4 px outline #0072B2 containing the text 1 tonne = 1,000 kg (48 px, bold, dark). Nothing else in the frame.

images.takeaway: 100 kg = 1 quintal, 10 quintals = 1 tonne, and so 1 tonne = 1,000 kg.
images.description: Five boxes from milligram to tonne joined by arrows, with 1,000 mg = 1 g, 1,000 g = 1 kg, 100 kg = 1 quintal, 10 quintals = 1 tonne.
images.context: Concept image for Quintal and Tonne. It follows the idea of the unit facts in your maths book (tiny to big) and shows the whole chain of units.
images.teaching_notes: Read the facts from left to right and say which unit is bigger each time. The slip to watch: thinking 1 quintal is 10 kg.

image_decisions.why: The chain shows how each unit links to the next, and that the tonne is 1,000 kg.
